# Introduction and System Context

This document defines the HuskySat-2 flight-software design and the interfaces between its software layers. It is written for a 3U CubeSat flight computer running Linux and F' (F Prime). The document introduces the software context first, then describes the Level 1 drivers, Level 2 hardware managers, Level 3 applications, and Level 4 system-services and control components.

HuskySat-2 uses optical-navigation experiments to validate the LOST, FOUND, and SCOPE algorithms.

The scope of this Software Design Document is the HuskySat-2 flight-software repository and the deployment architecture required to run it on the BeagleBone Black flight computer. It covers:

- software interfaces, ports, commands, events, telemetry, parameters, and state machines for components represented in this repository;
- Linux-backed Level 1 drivers and the Level 2 hardware managers that own device protocols and recovery behavior;
- Level 3 subsystem applications, ADCS algorithms, and the F' framework components used by the application topology;
- the intended decomposition of subsystem topologies and their cross-layer connections;
- integration of the LOST, FOUND, and SCOPE mission libraries; and
- the staged verification path from unit tests through GDS, subsystem, and integrated deployment testing.

The Level 4 system-services and control layer contains the satellite state machine, deployment-wide F' services, and fatal handling; hardware-reset ownership remains with the application-manager interfaces described in that layer.
